verdict.rationale: Kino's own agent takes natural-language requests ("Ask for the cut") and makes the edit on the timeline. It also exposes an MCP server so ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can search footage and edit projects from chat. A hands-on comparison found Kino easier to nudge and control than Claude Code alone, though another user found the results via Claude somewhat worse. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of supported command scope and limits, consistent independent corroboration of command reliability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Ask for the cut. The agent reads your footage, makes the edit, and leaves every clip on the timeline for you to move.
The desktop app runs an MCP server, so ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can search your footage and edit your projects from their own chat.
Manage many variants of your video and ask the agent to one-shot each.
